newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh begins commercial use of solar energy.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh begins commercial use of solar energy.

text.p: Power-starved Bangladesh on Thursday began commercial use of solar power when a photovoltaic plant lit hundreds of rural households in eastern Narshingdi district.
Energy Minister Nooruddin Khan switched on the plant which would initially provide power to some 1,000 households on a 29 square-kilometre island surrounded by the mighty Meghna river.
The $1.60 million plant would gradually cover 21 villages, the official BSS news agency said, quoting officials.
France has provided technical and financial assistance for the experimental project, they said.
Khan said if the project proved beneficial it would be replicated in other remote areas.
"Sun is abundant in Bangladesh, we have a huge potential for solar power. Outcome of the project will be very crucial," BSS quoted Energy Secretary Tawfiq Elahi Chowdhury as saying.
Only 17 percent of Bangladesh's 120 million people have access to electricity. The country produces 2,000 megawatts.
Bangladesh has recently opened power generation to foreign private investment to overcome a shortfall.
